newsitem.title: USA: Florida jobless rate edges down to 4.9 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Florida jobless rate edges down to 4.9 pct in May.

text.p: Florida's unemployment rate was 4.9 percnt in May, down from 5 percent in April and 5.1 percent a year ago, state Labor Secretary Doug Jamerson said Tuesday.
The data represent 351,000 unemployed Floridians out of a work force of 7.13 million.
Monroe County had the lowest unemployment rate in May, 2 percent, while Gulf County had the highest, 20 percent.
Of Florida's 67 counties, 37 saw decreases in their jobless rates from a year ago. Hamilton County had the larget decrease over the year, dropping by 3.1 percentage points to 6.1 percent.
Services added the most jobs over the year, 111,800, and saw the fastest growth rate, 5.3 percent.
Trade gained 55,900 jobs over the year for a 3.5 percent growth rate, while construction added 5,800 jobs and grew by 1.8 percent.

Manufacturing increased by 2,800 jobs or 0.6 percent. Transportation, communications and public utilities grew by 10,200 jobs or 3.3 percent. Finance, insurance and real estate grew by 12,900 jobs or 3.3 perent and government gained 19,800 jobs for a 2.1 percent growth rate over the year.

All of Florida's major metropolitan areas saw job increases over the year. Orlando added the most jobs, 41,800, and had the fastest growth rate, 5.6 percent. West Palm Beach added the fewest jobs, 15,500, while Miami had the slowest growth rate, 2.6 percent.
